title: Yet Another Attempt to Strangle Scientific Funding
body_text: I wrote not so long ago about the Trump administration’s plans to take over all aspects of federal scientific funding. That attempt seems to have been consigned to bureaucratic limbo after a torrent of negative comments poured in and Congress blocked it in the latest funding resolution, but the overall goal is not something that these people are going to forget about. As I said at the time, “The Trump administration hates academic science funding, full stop. They hate where that money goes, and they hate who it goes to. They want to keep all that money for themselves, to hand out to favored cronies who can help them get elected and to steer yet more money and more power back into their hands.” That has not changed one bit. The latest attempt is apparently to create some sort of executive-agency board that would have the final say on all NIH grants. Politico and the Washington Post seem to have been first to report this, in stories that included the unusual detail of Jay Bhattacharya objecting to the idea. I’m not sure what to make of that - details of Oval Office meetings do not leak for no reason, and the reasons (especially with this crowd) are almost invariably to make someone look good or to make someone else look bad. I’ve seen speculation that this is a way for Bhattacharya to buy some distance from what even he has to realize would be a massively unpopular process, and there’s also the possibility that he resents having some of his power as NIH Director taken from him and handed to (for example) Russell Vought. I have no idea, myself. But what is perfectly clear is how this idea is aligned perfectly with the administration’s approach - and for that, you can read “Russell Vought’s approach” and not lose anything in the restatement. The New York Times article on this says that “. . .some of Mr. Trump’s top lieutenants have expressed frustration about a perceived slowdown in the administration’s attempt to force conservative cultural changes on academia”. Harvard is a particular target of this stuff, and Trump’s people have already lost two lawsuits over the issue (with more in progress). The Times says that the Friday meeting was called in particular to ask why the NIH hasn’t been doing more in this line and they also say that the part about Jay Bhattacharya pushing back is “according to two people close to Dr. Bhattacharya”. Make of that what you will. If he is actually trying to keep this from happening, well, welcome to the resistance Dr. B. You’ve said and done a lot of awful things so far in your tenure, and (in common with so many other people in this administration) I make no secret of my opinion that you never should have been appointed to your position in the first place. Nothing will erase all this, and (in common with so many others in this administration) I don’t think that history is going to treat you very well at all. But if you can frustrate Russell Vought, even if it’s just in service of saving your own privileges or saving your own skin, then go to it, I say. I want to see as much disorganized infighting as possible in all parts of this administration. We may be looking at a fight between one faction that wants to see NIH funding severely beaten up and another faction that wants to see it completely killed, but in these degenerate times one has to take what one can get. This entire idea seems prima facie unconstitutional (Congress is in charge of determining how its appropriations are to be spent, not the Executive Branch) but that doesn’t seem to have been slowing people down much recently. Degenerate times, as I say. If Trump and his cronies continue on this topic, expect some sort of strained "National Security" rationale for it all - they seem to have decided that those are the magic words that will allow them to do whatever idiotic, destructive projects that cross their minds. Meanwhile, The Stand Up For Science folks have resources to help you let your Senators and Representatives know what you think of this latest idea, and remember: that’s what scuttled the last attempt at this kind of takeover. Make noise! Make it unpopular - in this election season that’s particularly effective. Show them that there’s a price to be paid. This is a president whose approval ratings are diving below 30%, and he's taking his party down with him. Let's get those numbers down even more!
